{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABiCUd5Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhLaGr0", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 401, "title": "Build the first standalone desktop app for local OS-wide voice typing and reusable graphs", "body": "## Problem

The product vision (#7) is a local-first composable processing system, not a browser extension alone. Today the Chrome extension and standalone Web Playground are the implemented hosts. There is no standalone desktop application that can run a saved processing graph and insert its text output into another desktop application's focused text field.

A browser is only one of the user's applications. Users who want quick browser-only use should continue to use the existing extension (or the installation-free standalone Web pages where applicable). Users who want OS-wide use should be able to install an independent desktop application and dictate into a browser, editor, chat application or another supported text field without having to install the browser extension or move focus to a transcription window.

The agreed first desktop UX is a resident tray/menu-bar application, a global shortcut, a small non-focus-stealing recording indicator, and a separate window for graph/model configuration. Do not make the existing Web experience dependent on this new application.

## Expected outcome

Deliver a **working first standalone desktop application (v1)**, not just a design document, mockup, command-line demo or empty desktop shell. Focus on the complete local voice-typing workflow and reuse the current graph system. Implement one desktop OS/environment end to end first; do not attempt every OS or mobile platform in this issue.

### 1. Platform and implementation boundary

- Select **one explicitly supported desktop OS/environment** at implementation time, based on the available automated build and OS-integration test environment, native focused-text insertion/capture capabilities and existing project dependencies. Record the choice and rationale in the PR and desktop guide. A Linux X11 session with virtual audio/display is a reasonable initial target if it provides the necessary automated native integration; do not claim Wayland, macOS or Windows support unless actually implemented and validated. Other platforms are follow-ups, not closure requirements.
- Provide a reproducible build and launchable standalone desktop package for the chosen target. A WebView/Electron/Tauri or other suitable desktop shell is acceptable if it meets the requirements; do not mandate a new language, rewrite the graph system, or require a native inference runtime solely for its own sake. Prefer the smallest coherent implementation and justify substantial dependencies.
- Share existing source code where practical and preserve the same typed Node/Port/Graph/Pipeline contracts, model identities and saved graph format. Isolate OS-specific capture, focused text output, shortcuts, permissions, window/tray and storage behind the smallest useful host boundaries. Do not copy the whole extension into a second divergent implementation or introduce a universal plugin SDK.
- **Share architecture and reusable code, not running resources across apps.** Desktop and browser hosts start, run and stop independently. Desktop owns its graph/settings storage, verified model-file cache, inference instances, memory/VRAM and session lifecycle. No required shared service, localhost daemon, native messaging, cross-app model cache, model process, account or synchronization. Browser-only users must not install or run any new desktop component. Simultaneous usage may use separate memory; resource contention must fail visibly and locally.
- The desktop UI/renderer must not gain arbitrary privileged OS access. Expose only the narrowly scoped host capabilities it needs; no unauthenticated local server, arbitrary shell commands, remote executable code, or broad privileged bridge. Speech/text is processed locally, with no cloud inference/telemetry or transcript upload.

### 2. Everyday UX: resident app and OS-wide dictation

- On launch, the desktop app has an OS-appropriate tray/menu-bar entry. Its compact menu exposes Start/Stop voice typing (state-dependent), selection of the saved graph used by the shortcut, Graph Library, Models, Settings and Quit. Keep graph selection stable and persisted. Closing the management window leaves the explicitly launched app resident; Quit actually releases owned resources and unregisters shortcuts. No auto-start at login requirement.
- Provide a discoverable default **global keyboard shortcut** (choose a reasonable non-conflicting default for the target OS) and allow editing it in Settings. Registration failures/conflicts are actionable; do not silently steal an existing binding. The shortcut toggles Start/Stop from another app without bringing the desktop management window forward.
- On the first intentional Start, obtain any required microphone or accessibility/input-injection permissions using normal OS mechanisms; do not bypass permissions or capture before user intent. Show preparation/readiness and permission errors accurately. Prepare verified local models before recording; a missing model must not silently trigger capture or cloud fallback.
- While capturing, show a compact, always-on-top **non-activating/non-focus-stealing** recording indicator with clear recording/stop affordance; indicate actual state, not merely shortcut press. Do not open a large transcription window for ordinary voice typing. The shortcut and indicator Stop action stop the same session; tray state stays consistent. Repeated/rapid presses must not create overlapping sessions.
- Typical flow: place a caret in another application's text field → invoke global shortcut → speak → committed recognized text is inserted at that target → invoke shortcut again to stop. Browser input fields must work through the desktop host even with no extension installed. Support at least one other independent desktop text editor as well.
- Use a supported OS text-insertion mechanism (not simulated typing through the app's own renderer). Insert accepted committed TEXT exactly once, in order, preserving Unicode, whitespace and newlines; no automatic Enter/Submit, command execution, arbitrary key sequences, silent clipboard loss or accidental replacement of unrelated text. If clipboard-based insertion is chosen, handle ownership/races and preserve unrelated clipboard data where safely possible. Document any unavoidable limitation.
- Bind a session to the authorized focused target at Start, revalidate its identity/editability before every insertion, and stop or safely reject output if the target, focus, permission or window disappears/changes. Never redirect late output into an unrelated newly focused application or protected/password field. If the host cannot establish a safe target, fail visibly rather than blindly injecting. Scope support to editable controls that can be safely identified on the selected OS; document unsupported controls. Stop should drain valid accepted final output only to the authorized target; Cancel/Quit/target invalidation must discard pending work, reject late callbacks and release capture/workers.

### 3. Actual graph, inference and management UI

- Supply a working default Japanese voice-typing graph using the existing **Moonshine Small Streaming Japanese** recognizer (or its compatible desktop execution adapter for the same pinned model):
  `Microphone → SpeechToTextMoonshineSmallJa.final → Focused Application Text Output`.
  Use the established PCM and TEXT contracts and real local model inference. Provisional hypotheses must not be repeatedly inserted into the target. A fixture/stub alone is not the delivered runtime.
- Implement the desktop microphone source and focused-application output as real graph endpoints, not a parallel hard-coded dictation path outside the Pipeline. The text sink accepts generic TEXT independently of producer/model identity. Preserve explicit composition so an intermediate supported deterministic text processor can be inserted without rewriting the host.
- Reuse the existing Graph Library, Graph Editor, Models and Live concepts and as much production UI/code as practical in the management window:
  - **Graph Library:** list, select, create/duplicate/edit and persist named desktop graphs; select which saved graph the shortcut launches. Provide graph JSON import/export using the existing schema and validate unsupported endpoints rather than silently migrating or discarding data.
  - **Graph Editor:** visually edit the default graph and other supported graphs with existing Node/Port behavior, Settings, validation, Auto Save and Undo/Redo. Include microphone, Japanese ASR, focused application TEXT output, Display and at least a useful existing deterministic text-processing node (e.g. TextFormatter). Unsupported browser-specific nodes or unported AI runtimes must not appear as executable desktop capabilities. Expose a clear supported subset, not all current extension nodes.
  - **Models:** local verified preparation/progress/retry/cancel/delete/readiness for the shipped ASR model; reuse pinned asset identities, checksums and license/notice rules as appropriate. Do not package large weights by default or redownload on each launch. With a prepared cache, run offline. Do not delete assets in active use. Any other existing model support is optional for v1; no requirement to port all translation/LLM/TTS models.
  - **Live:** the existing display pattern for graphs explicitly using Display, with a management/window view to start/stop and inspect output; voice typing itself must not require opening Live.
  - **Settings:** global shortcut and necessary desktop-specific settings/permission recovery only.
- A session uses the saved graph snapshot at Start; edits affect subsequent sessions. No hidden accumulation, rewiring, ASR-specific logic in the generic output sink, or forced Display path. Keep explicit graph validation and useful errors. Existing web graphs and browser storage must remain unaffected.
- Follow [README UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple; Show, don't tell; Intuitive and predictable**. Use layout, visual hierarchy and contextual controls rather than permanent instructional paragraphs or duplicate counters. Keep essential accessible names, visible focus, permission/error recovery and concise state indicators. Reuse existing Graph Editor input-control design from #398.

### 4. Explicitly out of scope

All-OS parity; mobile; system/tab audio capture outside the existing extension; porting every model, processor or extension-specific feature; cross-process model sharing/synchronization; login autostart; cloud backend; global inline mic icons in arbitrary apps; installer signing, app-store submission or public release/deployment; product-wide redesign. Do not weaken browser support to accommodate the desktop host. These are future issues when justified.

### Mandatory pre-merge acceptance (automated; no human gate)

Use the [test/CI principles](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-principles). Choose the initial desktop target and harness together so the following can be executed by an implementation agent in a real or virtual desktop session. Do not turn a missing human reviewer, physical device, microphone, subjective UX evaluation or user-installed-app test into an acceptance/closure dependency.

- [ ] Reproducible desktop build/package and automated launch of the actual desktop app on the documented supported target; verify normal tray/menu lifecycle, management-window close/residency and Quit cleanup. Test the real host/renderer boundary, not just a mock HTML page.
- [ ] Automated real desktop integration test invokes the registered global shortcut from an independent text target (e.g. a test editor/browser without extension), verifies focus is not stolen by the app/recording indicator, Start/Stop state is consistent, and committed Unicode TEXT reaches the intended target exactly once. Cover a separate desktop editor and an ordinary browser input using the actual OS output mechanism; a deterministic producer may provide TEXT for these focused integration tests.
- [ ] Exercise the real microphone capture path with a virtual/loopback audio input where appropriate and a checked-in/licensed deterministic speech fixture. Run at least one automated real-model smoke through the delivered local ASR runtime (pinned Japanese Moonshine) with known speech, showing genuine nonempty committed transcript and successful insertion/output through the real Pipeline; record fixture, actual output and model revision. No subjective recognition-quality threshold or physical microphone is necessary. Keep model downloads/cache reuse limited to the real smoke and use deterministic fixtures elsewhere; do not label stub results as real inference.
- [ ] Automated safety/lifecycle tests cover focus/target change and loss, unsupported or protected target, denied permission, shortcut conflicts, repeated Start/Stop, failure/Cancel/Quit, stale callbacks and no wrong-target/duplicate text. Use deterministic host fixtures for error branches difficult to trigger reliably at OS level, with actual OS-path coverage for normal behavior. Verify no unexpected submit and preservation of text boundaries/Unicode; clipboard-specific tests if used.
- [ ] Automated desktop graph UI/storage tests demonstrate selection, editing, persistence/reload, Undo/Redo, JSON round-trip, validation of unsupported nodes, explicit deterministic processor composition, Display/Live output and snapshot isolation. Verify model prepare/readiness/cancellation/reuse/deletion/error handling at the lightest meaningful layer; prepared offline ASR works. No mandatory heavyweight test for unrelated models.
- [ ] Verify the desktop package can operate without the extension and the existing extension/standalone browser hosts can operate with no desktop process installed/running. No cross-app resource dependency. Run `npm test` and applicable affected browser/MV3 regression checks, plus new desktop tests/build. Do not introduce regressions in the existing hosts or require their users to download a desktop executable.
- [ ] Add an English desktop setup/usage/architecture guide with supported OS/environment, build/run/test commands, permissions, supported controls and node subset, cache/storage isolation, shortcut behavior, limitations and follow-up scope; update README/architecture references so implemented vs future platforms are accurate. Record actual commands/results, evidence and test limitations in the PR; run `git diff --check`.

**No human confirmation is required to approve, merge or close this Issue.** Automated tests, a reproducible package and recorded evidence are the acceptance mechanism. Optional real-user/physical-microphone testing and subjective UX feedback are welcome later but are not a gate and must not keep or reopen an otherwise completed Issue. If mandatory automated validation is blocked, report the blocker truthfully and arrange an agent-executable environment; do not substitute a human approval request, mark an unexecuted check passed or claim unsupported platforms. Keep the normal `Closes #N` reference after implementation and mandatory checks are complete.

## Required post-merge verification

**None.** The first desktop package is built and verified before merge; public release, signing, store distribution and deployment are not part of this issue. No post-merge human validation or external approval is required.

## Context

- Parent vision: #7, [processing-pipeline platform direction](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/processing-pipeline.md#local-execution-and-platform-direction). Platform implementations may differ while contracts remain reusable; do not require a common runtime.
- Existing host and input behavior: [Chrome extension guide](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/chrome-extension.md), [Graph Editor and saved graph behavior](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/extension-graph.md), [portable Display items](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/display-items.md).
- Existing local ASR and verified assets: [Moonshine nodes](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/optional-asr-nodes.md), [model asset lifecycle](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/model-assets.md), [port contracts](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/port-contracts.md). Reuse production modules in `web/` and relevant existing editor/library modules in `extension/` where appropriate without depending on Chrome APIs in the desktop host.
- Follow the [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md) and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md). Use English collaboration artifacts; implementation → PR → review → merge and close the implemented Issue. Keep review and ordinary quality checks; do not add a human acceptance gate.
